Uzzielites
uh-ZEE-el-ites
n. pl. (the Levitical family of Uzziel, fourth son of Kohath)
Hebrew Uzzi'el, God is my strength, from oz, strength, with El, God; named once, Numbers 3:27.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Uzzielites are the last of the four Kohathite families: “And of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites” (Numbers 3:27). Their chief is named next: “And the chief of the house of the father of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel” (Numbers 3:30). Uzziel was Aaron's uncle, and it was his sons Mishael and Elzaphan whom Moses called to carry Nadab and Abihu out of the camp in their coats after the strange fire consumed them. The house of Uzziel was therefore the house that handled the bodies of the priests who died for offering what God had not commanded, and it did so under the strictest order Aaron ever received, forbidden to mourn. The name means God is my strength, and the family's recorded work was to bear away the evidence of what happens when a man draws near to the LORD on his own terms. In David's day the Uzzielites were still in service: Amminadab the chief of the sons of Uzziel came with a hundred and twelve of his brethren to bring up the ark, after the first attempt had cost Uzza his life.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): Uzzielites, the Levitical family of Uzziel, fourth son of Kohath, named once, Numbers 3:27; the name signifies God is my strength.

Hebrew Uzzi'el, God is my strength.

From oz, strength, with El, God.

It occurs once in the Authorized Version, Numbers 3:27.

The clan descends from Uzziel, fourth son of Kohath and uncle of Aaron.

Elizaphan the son of Uzziel was chief of the Kohathite houses.

Key Scripture

Num 3:27 — "And of Kohath was the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izeharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites: these are the families of the Kohathites."

Num 3:30 — "And the chief of the house of the father of the families of the Kohathites shall be Elizaphan the son of Uzziel."

Lev 10:4 — "And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and said unto them, Come near, carry your brethren from before the sanctuary out of the camp."

1Ch 15:10 — "Of the sons of Uzziel; Amminadab the chief, and his brethren an hundred and twelve."

Modern Corruption

The regulative principle is dismissed as rigidity; the house of Uzziel carried out the bodies of the two priests who worshipped God in a way He had not commanded.

expand to see more

Strange fire is the clearest case in Scripture for the regulative principle of worship, and the modern church has largely decided against it. Nadab and Abihu offered incense the LORD had not commanded them, and fire went out from before the LORD and devoured them. It was Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, who were called to carry them out of the camp. The innovation was not immoral by any ordinary reckoning; it was simply unauthorised, and that was the whole of the charge.

The Reformed and Baptist confessions hold that what God has not commanded in His worship is not permitted, and the Uzzielites are the family that cleared the ground after the point was made. The principle to recover is that acceptable worship is revealed, not devised. The same house was later trusted to carry the ark, and it did so by the appointed order after Uzza had died for touching it on a cart — the Levites bearing it on their shoulders, as the LORD had said.
